evidence: On PowerToys 0.101.2362, one snapshot after direct Alt+Win+V paste recorded LWin and LAlt down while other modifiers were up; a later snapshot showed all eight up.
The detailed report identifies try_inject_modifier_key_restore and later SendInput in AdvancedPasteModuleInterface/dllmain.cpp as a possible ordering race.
The critical ordering was not captured; Keyboard Manager was enabled and not isolated.
The report cites related #43220, #42471, and #50127 but does not establish this incident is handled.

proposed_fixes.title: Prevent stale modifier restoration after Advanced Paste
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Red hypothesis: the worker may sample Win/Alt as held, queue synthetic restore key-down input, then submit it after physical key-up, leaving logical modifiers down. The ordering is not captured.
plan: Instrument modifier restore decisions and requested/sent SendInput events for direct plain-text paste without collecting typed text or clipboard content.
Reproduce physical key release at different points between state sampling and SendInput; compare Keyboard Manager enabled and disabled.
If stale restore input is confirmed, avoid reasserting a modifier released before injection or verify release state at the established boundary.
Add focused tests for release-before-submit and normal held-modifier behavior.

known_information: The 2026-10-16 report documents two episodes; one snapshot recorded LWin and LAlt down, and a later snapshot showed all modifiers up.
Direct Advanced Paste Alt+Win+V activations were logged near the first episode.
The report identifies a possible modifier-restore then SendInput path in AdvancedPasteModuleInterface/dllmain.cpp.
Keyboard Manager was enabled with LWin+V mapped to LCtrl+V; disabling it was not tested.
The commenter states the ordering and continuous duration were not independently captured.
issue_context.analysis: The detailed evidence identifies a testable maintainer-side path. Do not ask for generic logs; instrument timing and separate logical-state observation from physical key state.
issue_context.summary: Advanced Paste plain-text paste may leave logical Win/Alt modifiers down after physical release; snapshots support the symptom but do not prove the proposed restore-input race.
initial_investigation: Reviewed full detailed issue comment, incident timestamps, snapshots, enabled mappings, source hypothesis, and collection limits.
No causal claim is inferred from clean logs or security software presence.
Related #43220, #42471, and #50127 are cited but do not prove this exact symptom is handled.
inferences: Synthetic Win/Alt key-down submitted after physical release could match the logical snapshot and tap-to-clear symptom, but this timing is unconfirmed.
Keyboard Manager may interact, but no conflict is established.
